title: Python 1 — Output a message to the screen
intro: Your first Python program, running right here in the browser.

blocks.title: Output a message to the screen
blocks.task: Read the explanation, run the code, then answer the questions underneath.

blocks.html:
To output something to the screen in Python, we use the print() function.

For example: print("Hello World!") will output the message Hello World!

blocks.title: Investigate
blocks.task: Run the code below, then add your own output message on line 3 to say "Learning to program".

blocks.prompt: What is the purpose of the print function?
How do you think you could get the user to type in something?

blocks.title: Asking the user a question
blocks.task: Run this one — the console will ask you for a name. Type it and press Enter.

blocks.title: Try it
blocks.starter:
name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Hello " + name)

blocks.prompt: What is the difference between print and input?

blocks.title: Drawing with code
blocks.task: Change the numbers to draw a triangle instead of a square.

blocks.title: Turtle
blocks.starter:
import turtle
t = turtle.Turtle()
t.color("blue")

for side in range(4):
    t.forward(100)
    t.right(90)
